dataText.v0: GWIS (Global Wildfire Information System), estimates of burned areas and number of fires
dataText.v1: Not a report. GWIS, the Global Wildfire Information System, makes this estimate by mapping the burned area it can see in satellite images world-wide, so small fires are missing.
dataText.v2: EFFIS (European Forest Fire Information System), estimates of burned areas and number of fires
dataText.v3: Not a report. EFFIS, the European Forest Fire Information System, makes this estimate by mapping the burned area it can see in satellite images, and it maps mainly fires of about 30 hectares or more, so smaller fires are missing.
dataText.v4: EFFIS annual report, Forest Fires in Europe, Middle East and North Africa 2024, Publications Office of the European Union, annex Tables 101 to 104 with Table 1 for 2024, source JRC's elaboration of the country reports
dataText.v5: What the countries' own national fire services reported, year by year, as the annex of the EFFIS annual report prints it (JRC's wording: its elaboration of the country reports). Each country counts fires and burned area by its own rules, so a fire its service does not record is missing and countries are not directly comparable.
dataText.v6: EFFIS annual report, Forest Fires in Europe, Middle East and North Africa 2024, Publications Office of the European Union, annex Tables 101 to 104 with Table 1 for 2024, source JRC's elaboration of the country reports, Table 2 for Bulgaria, and the Forest Agency 2025 report
dataText.v7: What the Executive Forest Agency reported for forest fires, from the EFFIS annual report annex and Bulgaria chapter, and the agency's 2025 report (https://www.iag.bg/data/docs/Doklad25_01str_final_08.05.2026.pdf, page 35). The latter revises the 2024 count to 565 from 595 and reports 546 fires on 154588 decares (15458.8 hectares) in 2025. For 2019, the EFFIS report's Table 2 gives 5619 hectares while its annex gives 5620; the Table 2 value is used. Fires on other land are missing.
dataText.v8: NIFC (National Interagency Fire Center), Total Wildland Fires and Acres (1983-2025), source the National Interagency Coordination Center
dataText.v9: What the National Interagency Coordination Center reported: all wildland fires and the area they burned, counted from the records of the federal and state wildland fire agencies, so a fire none of them recorded is missing. Acres in the source are converted to hectares, 1 acre = 0.40468564224 hectares. The source marks 2004 with an asterisk: 2004 fires and acres do not include state lands for North Carolina.

satellites.heading: Raw counts per satellite
satellites.caption: What each satellite measured, with no conversion applied.
satellites.countryOnly: Per-satellite counts are held for whole countries only.
satellites.note: An empty cell means the satellite was not in orbit or not measuring.

table.heading: The months as rows
table.caption: Every month in the calendar, in {unit}.
table.zeroNote: 0 means the satellites looked and saw no fire. "no data" means there was no measurement at all.

downloads.heading: Downloads
downloads.note: Every file starts with comment lines naming the place, the dates and the sources. An empty field means no measurement; 0 means no fire seen.
downloads.pngMissing: The picture is not on screen, so it could not be saved.
downloads.pngFailed: The picture could not be turned into a PNG in this browser.

hotspot.text: One satellite reading that a patch of ground was burning when the satellite passed over.

fireDay.text: One small square of ground counted on one day with fire, added up over the area, so a long fire counts more than a brief one.

anomaly.text: How far a month sits from the usual level for that same month in past years.

frp.text: Fire radiative power, in megawatts: how much heat the fire was giving off as the satellite passed.

harmonized.text: Older and newer satellites are brought to one scale, so a change in the record is a change on the ground.

estimated.text: A month before February 2012, worked out from the older MODIS satellites, with a lower and upper bound.

noData.text: Nothing was measured. Different from 0, which means the satellites looked and saw no fire.

searchDistance.text: How far from the chosen point the app keeps readings, from 0 to 500 km.
